expected_symptom: For code following a #line directive, DXIL debug metadata should name the directive's virtual line and file; instead !DILocation reports the physical line and the only !DIFile is the physical file. Scored as a presence (physical line 9 present) plus a self-test (pre-directive line 7 present), not as an absence.
summary: Reproduces on main (1.9.0.5433, public commit 13730886e) and on 19 of 20 stable releases: DXIL !DILocation/!DIFile carry the physical line and file for code after a #line directive. It is deliberate -- PR #2991 passes UseLineDirectives=false at four CGDebugInfo getPresumedLoc sites and shipped a test asserting it; adam-yang said so in-thread in 2022 and the reporter accepted the default, narrowing the ask to an opt-in flag. That flag does not exist: the only #line compile option is -ignore-line-directives, which moves the opposite way (it makes even diagnostics report the physical location), and -line-directive is rewriter-only. Measured contrast in one build on one source: diagnostics report virtual-source.hlsl:400:17 and -spirv -fspv-debug=line emits OpLine 400 against OpString virtual-source.hlsl, so only DXIL debug info uses the physical location; hlsl_clang_trunk on Compiler Explorer already emits !DILocation(line: 400) with !DIFile(filename: "virtual-source.hlsl"). The live item is therefore an enhancement (an opt-in flag), and whether to add it is a maintainer decision this triage does not pre-empt.
title: DXIL debug locations do not respect #line directives
